scientific.label: Ice absorption
scientific.title: Partial Cassini VIMS water-ice signature
scientific.description: Near-2.02 µm water-ice absorption in selected Cassini observations; not ice abundance.

transfer.interpretation: Trial acceptance bounds, not estimates of source accuracy. Every bilinear contributor must lie within two diagonal pixel footprints of the closest source-mesh point; a footprint is the pixel range times the camera pixel angle, stretched by the emission angle, about 0.66 km across the diagonal at nadir from 78,000 km. Emission is limited to 75 degrees. The closest point must lie within 1.07 km of the displayed mesh, its simplification error, and be visible from the refined camera in the full mesh.

metadata.label: ISS photograph
metadata.coverage: One Cassini narrow-angle clear-filter photograph from the approach of 11 June 2004 at 0.47 km per pixel and 86 degrees phase, projected onto the 2023 SPC shape through a camera derived from Cassini SPICE kernels and refined to the limb. Only the sunlit half of the disc is used. Grid marks surface the camera did not see or that lay in shadow. Brightness is disk-normalized with an empirical Lommel-Seeliger law; it is not measured albedo.

celestial.sunSource: JPL Phoebe orbit and the retained Gaskell source-model orientation; the 2023 release uses the same image/kernel set and shifts its origin to the center of figure. Present-day rotation phase is not independently qualified.

controls.label: Relative albedo
controls.notes: Relative brightness from the 2023 Cassini shape/albedo model, normalized near one; not natural color or measured geometric albedo. Cells with fewer than five images or no maplet are marked missing. The 3,500-face display approximates the source shape; map detail is finer than the displayed geometry.

controls.label: ISS photograph
controls.notes: One Cassini narrow-angle photograph from the June 2004 approach, projected onto the shape model through a camera derived from Cassini SPICE kernels and refined to the limb. Only the sunlit half of the disc is used, so grid marks surface the camera did not see or that lay in shadow. Brightness is disk-normalized with an empirical Lommel-Seeliger law; it is not measured albedo.

controls.label: Radial height
controls.notes: Q512 model radius minus a 106.5 km sphere, in km; not a geoid or independent altimetry. The paired 2023 model is less certain in poorly imaged regions; unsupported cells are marked. The 3,500-face display approximates the source shape; map detail is finer than the displayed geometry.

controls.label: Maplet resolution
controls.notes: Finest contributing SPC maplet spacing in each 1° cell, in m/vertex. Smaller values mean finer local input, not guaranteed height accuracy. Cells without a maplet are marked missing.

controls.label: Image count
controls.notes: Contributing image count in each 1° source cell. Zero remains visible; fewer than five images warrants caution. Many images can share viewing geometry, so count alone does not establish accuracy.

controls.label: Infrared
controls.notes: A small region from Cassini’s 11 June 2004 flyby, supported by 41 original VIMS pixels. False color assigns red to about 2.02 µm, green to 1.59 µm and blue to 1.28 µm. All three channels share a 0–0.03 I/F display range and gamma 2.2; this stretch changes the display only. No photometric correction is applied, so illumination remains. Archive noise filtering and local replacement are retained; original detector defects and potentially affected neighbors are excluded. Gray grid marks unsupported areas and scan gaps. Placement is coarse on the existing shape, with several-kilometer spatial uncertainty. Fine surface positions are not established.

controls.label: Ice absorption
controls.notes: Near-2.02 µm water-ice band depth relative to a linear 1.82–2.20 µm continuum, using 41 original VIMS pixels from one small region in Cassini’s 11 June 2004 flyby. This measures absorption strength, not ice abundance. Viewing angle, grain size and noise also affect the values; no photometric correction is applied. Archive noise filtering and local replacement remain; original detector defects and potentially affected neighbors are excluded. Display colors saturate outside 0.1–0.3; original numerical values are retained. Gray grid marks unsupported areas and scan gaps. The region is placed coarsely on the existing shape, with several-kilometer spatial uncertainty.
